findings.title: Pydantic AI published a cluster of web-fetch, telemetry-redaction, local-agent, and concurrency vulnerabilities
visible_dates: CVE Services datePublished range for grouped CVEs: 2026-10-08T15:12:26.597Z through 2026-10-08T17:02:36.718Z
NVD publication timestamps for grouped CVEs: 2026-10-08T15:17:40.753 through 2026-10-08T17:17:15.237
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: pydantic-ai and pydantic-ai-slim ranges vary by CVE: 0.3.4 through pre-1.107.x for telemetry redaction paths, 1.34.0 through pre-2.30.0 for local web UI DNS-rebinding/request paths, 1.77.0 through pre-1.107.x/2.x for local WebFetch/web_fetch_tool resource-control and blocked-domain issues, and 2.10.0 through pre-2.53.0 for concurrency limiter streaming slots.
findings.summary: The October 8 Pydantic AI disclosures describe multiple concrete security boundaries: attacker-influenced local web fetches can bypass blocked domains or consume CPU/memory, opt-in local access can bypass IPv6 cloud-metadata blocking, OpenTelemetry redaction settings can still leak agent content through exception/retry fields, local developer chat endpoints can be reached through browser-origin paths, and streaming cleanup can retain concurrency slots.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Pydantic AI is an agent/application framework; these records affect model-directed URL fetching, cloud credential exposure, local developer agent authority, telemetry confidentiality, and availability gates around shared model execution.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad Pydantic AI framework/product context.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep local coverage focused on URL-fetch SSRF/resource controls, telemetry redaction bypasses, local-agent web authority, and affected/fixed version gates.

findings.title: Obot disclosed MCP catalog credential exposure and vMCP prompt/resource authorization bypasses
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Obot 0.12.0 before 0.26.2 for MCP catalog credential exposure; Obot 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 for vMCP profile prompt/resource authorization bypass.
findings.summary: One Obot record allows authenticated users to read plaintext static secrets from MCP catalog entries granted by access-control rules; the other lets authenticated users matching a vMCP profile reach prompts and resources of ungranted components because profiles were enforced only for tools.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP catalog entries, prompts, resources, and vMCP profiles are delegated-agent authority boundaries; credential disclosure and prompt/resource overreach can let ordinary users move from permitted tools into backend secrets or ungranted context.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad Obot/product catalog context if needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the MCP credential and vMCP authorization boundaries in this wiki.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from CVE Services records with GitHub advisory and release references. Local search found no prior raw/docs/wiki mention of these CVEs.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether credential exposure and prompt/resource bypass need separate leaves under identity-and-access and data-and-privacy.
Verify whether v0.26.2 fully fixes both boundaries before writing steady-state guidance.

findings.title: Splunk MCP Server advisory describes custom API tool SSRF and token exposure
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Splunk MCP Server 1.2 below fixed version 1.2.1; custom API tool REST API; mcp_tool_admin and mcp_tool_execute role capabilities.
findings.summary: Splunk says a user with mcp_tool_admin could configure a custom API tool to send requests to an attacker-controlled URL, and a user with mcp_tool_execute who runs that tool could expose their Splunk platform authentication token to the configured URL.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is an MCP tool-governance and delegated-authority failure: a configured tool can cause a later executor's platform token to cross a trust boundary controlled by another user.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad Splunk/product context if needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the MCP custom tool, SSRF, token-forwarding, and role-capability boundaries local.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from Splunk's official advisory archive plus CVE Services/NVD timing. Direct SVD page returned an internal error, but the advisory archive exposes the full SVD-2026-1004 row.

findings.title: BeamMCP disclosed schema-enforcement and boolean/null normalization flaws
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ScriptKittyOS beam_mcp from 0.1.0 before 0.10.1; the records also cite commit 083838eb8e17fe5f6fcaf761bdbe203110288b0b as affected.
findings.summary: BeamMCP accepted MCP client arguments that violated advertised nested schema constraints, and normalized JSON true, false, and null into string values before host dispatch. A host that relied on advertised schema or boolean false semantics could receive values that crossed its policy or execution assumptions.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP tools/list schemas are part of the contract between agent clients and tool hosts. If the server advertises constraints it does not enforce, policy layers and host dispatch code may authorize or execute tool calls under false assumptions.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad MCP framework/server catalog context if needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep schema-enforcement, argument-normalization, and policy-bypass implications local.

findings.title: Banks prompt template package disclosed prompt-registry symlink and privileged-message injection flaws
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: masci/banks before 2.5.1 for DirectoryPromptRegistry symlink traversal/file disclosure-overwrite; before 2.5.0 for ChatMessage parsing of rendered untrusted prompt output.
findings.summary: Banks DirectoryPromptRegistry could follow symlinks for index.json or .jinja files outside the registry root, enabling file disclosure or overwrite when attackers influence a prompt directory. Separately, rendered untrusted data passed to Prompt.chat_messages() could be parsed as ChatMessage JSON with arbitrary roles, crossing a prompt boundary into system, assistant, or tool messages.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prompt templates and prompt registries are AI supply-chain artifacts. File-boundary bypasses and user-controlled privileged chat messages can alter instructions, disclose local prompt assets, or confuse downstream tool/message handling.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad prompt-template package context if needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep prompt-boundary, prompt-registry, symlink traversal, and privileged message injection implications local.

findings.title: LangChain.js MongoDBChatMessageHistory advisory entered GitHub Advisory Database with cross-session access impact
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: @langchain/mongodb <= 1.3.0 fixed in 1.3.1; LangChain.js affected range also recorded by NVD as langchain-ai/langchainjs before 1.5.14.
findings.summary: MongoDBChatMessageHistory did not enforce session identifiers as strings at runtime, so untrusted structured identifiers could be interpreted as MongoDB query conditions. Affected multi-user shared-collection deployments may allow attackers to read, modify, or delete other users' stored conversations.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Stored chat history is an AI memory/data boundary. Query injection against session identifiers can turn an LLM application's conversation store into cross-tenant read/write access.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad LangChain/LangChain.js framework context.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the chat-history data isolation and MongoDB query injection boundary local.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for GitHub Advisory Database's October 8 in-window publication/review/update; NVD publication is just before the exact cutoff, so qualification relies on the in-window GitHub Advisory Database event.

findings.title: LatePoint AI Abilities API advisory reports cross-agent data disclosure and modification
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Appointment Booking Plugin / LatePoint before 5.6.9 when the AI Abilities API feature is enabled; authenticated LatePoint Agent role and above.
findings.summary: The advisory says several AI Abilities API actions did not enforce per-record authorization, allowing a LatePoint Agent-role user to read or modify other agents' profiles and read other agents' bookings and customer details.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is an AI-feature API authorization boundary: agent-facing automation actions can expose or modify booking/customer data outside the user's intended record scope.
